scope: advancing serverTime across snapshots does NOT dismiss the loader - another negative result, and the last cheap lever available

the_experiment.method: eight copies of the accepted body with serverTime stepping 72200, 72450, ... 73950, rotated by --snapshot-interval 2.0

conclusion: the world clock advancing does not satisfy the loader
so the frontend's load task is not waiting for server time to progress
together with the earlier negatives (flags byte, section set, entity content, entity ordering) this closes the set of snapshot-side levers that a server can pull
the_full_list_of_negatives: core snapshot contents (playerState fields, entity count, id, delta, position): accepted, loader never clears
flags byte 0x0C -> 0x08 (the exact baseline value cols writes): no change
an entity-free snapshot followed by entity snapshots: net 10 and count 1 coexist, ui_state stays 5
all five content blocks covered: already the case
advancing serverTime across eight snapshots: no change
what_remains: the loader object is partially initialised (0xBAADF00D in two slots) and is a C++ instance of at least 0x4F8 bytes with vtable 0xD599DC
identifying what fills those slots needs symbolic information for this build or a memory-write breakpoint, neither of which the current harness offers (fixed-address int3 only)
so the remaining work is a tooling problem as much as an investigative one
